title: A time column on Oracle is a TIMESTAMP(0), sent as epoch milliseconds
symptom: Round 1's SQL stopped at DimTime's first statement (a time written as '00:21:40'); the source side read the column back as 01-JAN-70 12.00.00 AM
cause: Oracle has no TIME type, so a model's time becomes TIMESTAMP(0) on 1970-01-01; Debezium sends it as epoch milliseconds
effect: A schema moved to Oracle from a database with TIME needs time literals as timestamps, and silver must decode the column as milliseconds to get the time of day
fix: Write TIMESTAMP '1970-01-01 hh:mm:ss'; read it with TO_CHAR(x, 'HH24:MI:SS'); give silver's schema the column precision 0
